verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Lean states the three facts for an abstract common-cover `Geometry` rather than in the manuscript's matrix notation; the rewriting is routine. (i) `path_eq_affine` says H ↦ H_w (w = eta held fixed) is affine with linear part `pathLinear = pointLinear ∘ horizontal ∘ coordinateLinear`. Because `pointLinear = coverPower^gap⁻¹ ∘ basis` and `coordinateLinear = basis.symm ∘ coverPower^gap` are mutually inverse and `horizontal z = (z.1, 0) = z - (0, z.2)`, one gets pathLinear Y = Y - (coordinateLinear Y).2 • pointLinear (0,1), i.e. exactly I₂ - v_t λ_t, with v_t = pointLinear (0,1) = T_g^{-(i-i₀)} c_i v_t and λ_t = (coordinateLinear ·).2. (ii) D_H^a H_w = 0 for a ≥ 2 is the affineness itself; no declaration states the vanishing second derivative separately — the Lean consumes it through the affine jet bounds (`norm_iteratedFDeriv_affine_le`, `sourceArgument_jet_bound`). (iii) `coordinates_eq_affine` gives D_H v = (coordinateLinear ·).2, and for the manuscript geometry `bandGeometry` (basis = B ∘ (z ↦ (z.1, c_i z.2)), coverPower^gap = T_g^{i-i₀} on the transverse direction) that second component is T_g^{i-i₀} λ_t / c_i; the size clause '= O(S_*)' is `bandGeometry_argumentCost_le`, which bounds argumentCost — hence ‖coordinateLinear‖ — by a constant fixed before the band, copy and source, times `ChartScales.S n`.
